Species identification cards and photos

Source: vignettes/articles/species-cards.Rmd
species-cards.Rmd

Each predator in the dashboard gets a card with a photo and a short description. dv_species_card_assets() finds those for one predator and returns the photo as a data URI, so the dashboard stays a single file. Cards exist for predators only; prey have no cards.

The examples use the predators of the public ICES stomach data that ship with the package (ICES Stomach Content Database, ICES, Copenhagen; extract distributed with the R package stomachr, Lindmark 2026; see ?ices_diet). The offline chunks run, with stand-in images drawn in a temporary folder; the chunks that go online are shown but not run.

library(DietView)

# drop non-food items and nematodes (mostly parasites, not prey)
phylum <- ices_lineage$phylum[match(ices_diet$prey_aphia_id, ices_lineage$prey_aphia_id)]
dat <- ices_diet[ices_diet$item_type != "non_food" & !phylum %in% "Nematoda", ]

spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_common",
  predator_latin = "predator_latin",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "prey_aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "prey_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight_g",
  count          = "prey_count",
  digestion      = "digestion_label",
  covariates     = c("region", "year", "quarter")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                   verbose = FALSE)

# the predators that will get a card, with the Latin names used online
unique(dat[dat$predator_common %in% c("Atlantic cod", "Whiting",
                                      "European plaice", "Atlantic mackerel"),
           c("predator_common", "predator_latin")])
#>        predator_common        predator_latin
#> 1              Whiting  Merlangius merlangus
#> 18        Atlantic cod          Gadus morhua
#> 162  Atlantic mackerel      Scomber scombrus
#> 6491   European plaice Pleuronectes platessa

Where the photo comes from

DietView takes the first photo it finds, in this order:

  1. a local file you name in species_info;
  2. a local file in image_dir named after the predator (atlantic_cod.jpg);
  3. a local file in image_dir named after its Latin name (gadus_morhua.jpg);
  4. with photo_source = "inaturalist", a photo of the taxon on iNaturalist, if its license is one you accept;
  5. with photo_source = "wikipedia", a Wikimedia Commons file you name, or the image of the Wikipedia article, if it is hosted on Commons.

File names are the name in lower case with every run of other characters replaced by _, and the extension is .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp. The default, photo_source = "none", never goes online. You can name both online sources, tried in the order given: photo_source = c("inaturalist", "wikipedia") uses Wikimedia Commons only for predators with no acceptable photo on iNaturalist.

The description is the text you give in species_info. Otherwise, with either online source, it is the summary of the taxon’s Wikipedia article (iNaturalist returns the same summary). Wikipedia text is under CC BY-SA, so the card credits it under the description. If a network lookup fails, the card is built without that element.

Your own photos, offline

With your own photos nothing is fetched. Here four stand-in images play the part of your photographs; in a real project they are files you took or licensed:

img_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "ices-cards")
dir.create(img_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

stand_in <- function(file, label) {
  grDevices::png(file, width = 400, height = 250)
  op <- graphics::par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  graphics::plot.new()
  graphics::rect(0, 0, 1, 1, col = "#dfe9f3", border = NA)
  graphics::text(0.5, 0.5, label, cex = 2)
  graphics::par(op)
  grDevices::dev.off()
}
stand_in(file.path(img_dir, "atlantic_cod.png"), "Atlantic cod")     # common name
#> agg_png 
#>       2
stand_in(file.path(img_dir, "merlangius_merlangus.png"), "Whiting")  # Latin name
#> agg_png 
#>       2
stand_in(file.path(img_dir, "plaice_photo.png"), "European plaice")  # any name
#> agg_png 
#>       2
list.files(img_dir)
#> [1] "atlantic_cod.png"         "merlangius_merlangus.png"
#> [3] "plaice_photo.png"

A photo carries its credit in one of two places. In species_info, next to the description:

info <- list(
  "Atlantic cod" = list(
    desc    = "Demersal gadid; small cod eat mostly crustaceans, large cod mostly fish.",
    author  = "Survey photographer",
    license = "CC BY"
  ),
  "European plaice" = list(
    desc    = "Right-eyed flatfish of sandy bottoms; feeds on polychaetes, bivalves and brittle stars.",
    photo   = file.path(img_dir, "plaice_photo.png"),
    credit  = "Photo: survey archive, used with permission"
  )
)

Or in a .json file with the same name as the image, which travels with it:

writeLines('{"author": "Jane Doe", "license": "CC BY-SA",
  "url": "https://www.example.org/photos/whiting"}',
  file.path(img_dir, "merlangius_merlangus.json"))

Now resolve each card, offline:

cards <- lapply(c("Atlantic cod", "Whiting", "European plaice", "Atlantic mackerel"),
  function(p) {
    latin <- dat$predator_latin[match(p, dat$predator_common)]
    a <- dv_species_card_assets(p, latin, info = info[[p]], image_dir = img_dir)
    data.frame(predator = p,
               photo    = if (is.null(a$path)) NA else basename(a$path),
               source   = if (is.null(a$source)) NA else a$source,
               credit   = if (is.null(a$credit)) NA else a$credit)
  })
do.call(rbind, cards)
#>            predator                    photo source
#> 1      Atlantic cod         atlantic_cod.png  local
#> 2           Whiting merlangius_merlangus.png  local
#> 3   European plaice         plaice_photo.png  local
#> 4 Atlantic mackerel                     <NA>   <NA>
#>                                        credit
#> 1           Photo: Survey photographer, CC BY
#> 2                   Photo: Jane Doe, CC BY-SA
#> 3 Photo: survey archive, used with permission
#> 4                                        <NA>

Cod is found by its common name and whiting by its Latin name; the plaice photo is the file named in species_info. The credit line is built from author and license when you do not write it yourself, and taken from the .json file for whiting. Mackerel has no file and no online source, so its card has no photo: the card is still built, with the stomach count and the length range.

The same species_info and image_dir go to the dashboard, which calls dv_species_card_assets() for every predator. Here for the four predators, one band and no strata, to keep the file small:

four <- c("Atlantic cod", "Whiting", "European plaice", "Atlantic mackerel")
prep4 <- dv_prepare(dat[dat$predator_common %in% four, ], spec,
                    taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage, verbose = FALSE)
out <- dv_build_html(prep4, output = file.path(tempdir(), "ices_cards.html"),
                     strata = character(0), bands = "occurrence",
                     species_info = info, image_dir = img_dir,
                     length_col = "length_cm", self_contained = FALSE)
html <- paste(readLines(out, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
c(photos_embedded = lengths(regmatches(html, gregexpr("data:image/png;base64", html))),
  whiting_credit  = grepl("Photo: Jane Doe, CC BY-SA", html, fixed = TRUE))
#> photos_embedded  whiting_credit 
#>               3               1

Three photos are embedded in the file and each card shows its credit line, linked to the photo’s page when a url is given.

Photos from iNaturalist

iNaturalist photos belong to the observers who took them, and each one carries its own license. DietView looks the predator up by its Latin name, keeps only a taxon whose name matches it, and tries the taxon’s default photo first, then its other photos, until one has a license you accept.

asset <- dv_species_card_assets(
  predator = "Atlantic cod", latin = "Gadus morhua",
  photo_source = "inaturalist",
  image_dir = "images")        # a permanent folder keeps the photos

asset$credit    # "Photo: <author>, CC BY, via iNaturalist"
asset$author    # the photographer
asset$license   # "CC0", "CC BY" or "CC BY-SA" by default
asset$url       # the photo's page on iNaturalist

By default only three licenses are accepted: CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA. Each one lets you redistribute the photo inside a dashboard, provided you credit the author, and for CC BY-SA keep the same license. Photos marked “all rights reserved” are never used. Many iNaturalist photos are CC BY-NC (no commercial use); accept them only if every use of the dashboard will be non-commercial:

dv_build_html(prep, output = "ices_dashboard.html",
              photo_source = "inaturalist",
              licenses = c("cc0", "cc-by", "cc-by-sa", "cc-by-nc"),
              image_dir = "images")

The other codes are "cc-by-nc-sa", "cc-by-nd" and "cc-by-nc-nd". If no photo of the taxon has an accepted license, the card has no photo.

On the card, the credit line sits under the photo and links to the photo’s page on iNaturalist. Each downloaded photo is saved in image_dir together with a .json file holding its source, author, license and page, so a photo reused in a later session keeps its credit. To fetch a photo again, delete the image and its .json file.

Photos from Wikimedia Commons

With photo_source = "wikipedia", DietView takes the image of the Wikipedia article for the Latin name, and uses it only if it is a Wikimedia Commons file whose license Commons reports; images hosted outside Commons, which may be non-free, are never used. To choose the file yourself, name it in species_info:

info_online <- list(
  "European plaice" = list(commons_file = "File:Pleuronectes platessa.jpg")
)
dv_species_card_assets("European plaice", latin = "Pleuronectes platessa",
                       info = info_online[["European plaice"]],
                       photo_source = "wikipedia", image_dir = "images")

The file name above is an example: check on Commons that the file exists, that it shows the species, and that its license suits your use. The credit line then names the author and the license reported by Commons.

Before you share a dashboard

The photos are embedded in the HTML file, so the file keeps working when image_dir is deleted, and it carries the photos wherever it goes. Open the dashboard and check the credit line on every card. A photo with no credit line is one you supplied without author or license.
